referees.quote: Several alternative explanations, such as conventional charge trapping or doping-induced phase shifts, need to be more rigorously excluded to support the claims of PNR-mediated memory.
I have several concerns that should be addressed to strengthen the manuscript support its conclusions. ... it would be essential to provide data on multiple devices
In conclusion, I could not recommend publishing the manuscript in its current form in Nature Communications before addressing all these concerns.
I co-reviewed this manuscript with one of the reviewers who provided the listed reports.

note: Recommendations are from Version 0, the first round in this file. There is no sign of a transfer from another journal. None of the first-round referees used the scale terms, so all levels are inferred. R1 and R2 asked for substantial new data: retention and decay curves, Hc2, wavelength-dependent illumination, multiple devices and low-leakage devices. R3 asked for controls, baseline-write-erase-rewrite R(T) data and thermal/wavelength checks. R3's wording ('not ... in its current form ... before addressing') conditions publication on revision rather than rejecting outright, so it is coded major revision. R4 is an Early Career co-reviewer who co-signed one of the other reports without saying which one. Because R1-R3 were all coded major revision, R4 gets the same level either way. In later rounds, R1 recommended acceptance in Version 1, and R2 and R3 recommended publication by Version 2.
